title: Screens You Order — and When You Stop

questions.stem: Before the first low-dose lung-cancer scan, the record should include:

options.text: Only the appointment time
The shared-decision conversation: benefit, harm, and false positives
A signed refusal of all future care
A colonoscopy referral

questions.explanation: Document the shared decision before the first scan.

options.text: The day after the first normal scan
Fifteen years after the last cigarette, or earlier if the patient would not act on a finding
Never, even after three decades of abstinence
Only on the patient's birthday

questions.explanation: Stopping is tied to fifteen years after the last cigarette, and to whether the patient would act on a finding.

questions.stem: Cervical screening may stop at sixty-five only when:

options.text: The patient turns sixty-five, regardless of records
Recent tests were adequate and negative
The patient asks once
There is a single missing Pap from twenty years ago

questions.explanation: Age alone does not stop the screen. Missing records are not a reason to stop.

questions.stem: A 65-year-old with no cervical-screening records. The next step is:

options.text: Stop because of age
Do not stop on age alone; get the tests or the records first
Order mammography instead
Start high-risk virus testing alone and discharge

questions.explanation: A patient with no records is not stopped.

questions.stem: High-risk virus testing alone for cervical screening, before age thirty:

options.text: Is the preferred stand-alone test
Should not be ordered alone in that age band
Replaces shared decision for lung screening
Is required at seventy-five

questions.explanation: Do not order high-risk virus testing alone before age thirty.

questions.stem: Mammography at seventy-five and older is:

options.text: An automatic yearly order for everyone
A decision, not an automatic order
Forbidden in all cases
Replaced by lung screening

questions.explanation: The evidence is not automatic at that age. It is a conversation.

questions.stem: Colon screening from seventy-six to eighty-five is:

options.text: Automatic in every healthy and every frail patient alike
Selective, not automatic
Never considered
The same as a therapeutic colonoscopy required by law

questions.explanation: In that age band, screening is a decision, not a standing order.

questions.stem: A screening test the patient would not act on (no biopsy, no treatment) should be:

options.text: Ordered anyway, for completeness
Not ordered
Replaced with three other screening tests
Hidden from the record

questions.explanation: Do not order a screening test if the patient would not accept the next step.

questions.stem: The lung-screening stop rule taught here is tied most tightly to:

options.text: The last normal chest film only
Fifteen years after the last cigarette
A single episode of bronchitis
The date of the last colon exam

questions.explanation: The fifteen-year clock after the last cigarette is the stop rule that was taught.

questions.stem: At seventy-five, a clinician orders a screening mammogram without a conversation because 'that is the protocol.' That approach is:

options.text: Required
Not supported; it is a decision, not an automatic order
The same as cervical screening at twenty-one
The same as a therapeutic biopsy

questions.explanation: Mammography at seventy-five and older is a decision, not an automatic order.
